Hard-gate investigation of the 2015 persistence-RMSE anomaly (0.898 vs 0.51-0.63 in 2002-2014), notebooks/02_forecastability.ipynb section 7-8. Ruled out partial-year/seasonal-composition artifact directly (pooled 2002-2014 Jan-Aug vs Sep-Dec persistence RMSE ratio only 1.03, far too small to explain the jump). Found the elevation is episodic within 2015 (Jan/Feb/Mar/Jun/Jul elevated 1.6-2.1x normal; Apr/May/Aug normal), broad-based not outlier-driven (1%-trimmed RMSE barely moves, median abs residual roughly doubles), global not regional (both hemispheres elevated similarly in worst month, Feb), and directional not just noisier (systematic negative mean-residual shift). Sourced cross-reference to the 2015-16 El Nino event (comparable in strength to 1997-98, documented global TWS/drought anomalies) offers a plausible physical explanation, not verified month-by-month against an ENSO index. VERDICT: genuine regime characteristic, not an artifact -- do not discard/down-weight 2015, but do not assume 2002-2014 volatility is representative of the Sep2015-Dec2018 test period either. Docs updated: ASSUMPTIONS.md A-004 upgraded Active-under-investigation to Validated (with caveat), new A-007 added for the El Nino hypothesis specifically (Active, pending ENSO-index verification), PROJECT_PLAN.md Experiment 2 checkbox marked complete with full findings.

notes: Highest-priority Phase 1 experiment per PROJECT_PLAN.md. notebooks/02_forecastability.ipynb section 9-10. Simulated 15 overlapping contiguous artificial blackout windows (K=9 months staleness) on the verified gap-free 2004-2010 training span, robustness-checked against a strictly non-overlapping independent subset (curve shape confirmed stable). Pooled RMSE grows 0.537 (k=1) to 0.884 (k=9), 1.65x. Stratified by 4 factors as required: (1) per-location ACF(1) quartile -- dominant factor, 0.403 RMSE spread at k=9; low-ACF locations worse in absolute terms at every horizon (0.769->1.015, 1.32x growth) but high-ACF locations degrade proportionally faster (0.284->0.611, 2.15x growth), a more nuanced pattern than PROJECT_PLAN.md's original illustrative sketch; (2) latitude band -- 0.191 spread, 0-30S is a severe outlier (0.495->1.033, 2.09x), plausibly linked to the same tropical/equatorial regions flagged in EXP-002's El Nino cross-reference; (3) season (N-hemisphere convention) -- weak, 0.079 spread; (4) drought regime at blackout onset (SPEI_12) -- weak but directionally consistent with notebook 01's mean-reversion finding, 0.066 spread, locations already in drought/wet extremes degrade faster than near-normal ones. AR(1) theoretical model validates curve shape/ordering but systematically over-predicts absolute error, indicating exploitable structure beyond lag-1 persistence. New finding: per-month grid incompleteness (previously found in Test.csv, EXP-001) also holds for Train.csv, even within the gap-free 2004-2010 span. Docs updated: ASSUMPTIONS.md new A-008 (Validated) formalizing ACF/historical-signature features as Phase 4's top-priority category, COMPETITIVE_ANALYSIS.md Section 16 priority list updated, PROJECT_PLAN.md Experiment 3 checkbox marked complete with full findings.

model: Baselines A/B/C/D (oracle persistence / last-known-state / seasonal climatology / hybrid)
notes: notebooks/02_forecastability.ipynb section 11-12. Corrected a subtle staleness-definition bug before computing anything: staleness must be measured to the TARGET month (row_month+1, per DATA_DICTIONARY.md's target definition), not the row's own month -- numerically coincides with Experiment 3's existing k convention, so Experiment 3's curve could be reused directly rather than re-derived. Reconstructed the real 18-month test temporal structure (6 FULL + 12 BLACKOUT offsets); the 12 real blackout months carry staleness-to-target k=2 through k=7, not a fixed value (distribution: k=2x4, k=3x3, k=4x2, k=5/6/7x1 each). Two independent methods cross-validate closely: Method A (reweighting Experiment 3's already-validated RMSE(k) curve by this real distribution) gives RMSE=0.7091 (equal-weight) / 0.7090 (row-count-weighted); Method B (direct replay of the exact real 41-month temporal pattern onto 8 independent windows of the verified clean 2004-2010 span, ground-truth scored) gives Baseline A (oracle, FULL months) RMSE=0.5247 (n=747,365), Baseline B (last-known, BLACKOUT months) RMSE=0.7145 (n=1,491,960), Baseline D (Hybrid, all 18 months) RMSE=0.6573 (n=2,239,325). Methods A and B agree within 0.005 pooled and 0.028 mean-abs per-offset (max 0.064) -- strong cross-validation, not coincidence. VERDICT: the in-sample persistence RMSE (0.572, Baseline A) is NOT the real naive floor for this competition's actual test structure, since 12/18 test months (66.7%) have no current TWS observation; Baseline D (0.6573) is the realistic 'do nothing clever' floor. Docs updated: ASSUMPTIONS.md new A-009 (Validated) formalizing this finding, COMPETITIVE_ANALYSIS.md Section 6 internal-targets table given added context reframing the 0.572 threshold, PROJECT_PLAN.md Experiment 4 checkbox marked complete with full findings.

model: Regression + AR(1) theoretical model (informing StateSnapshot schema)
notes: notebooks/02_forecastability.ipynb section 13-14. Tested whether per-location ACF(1) explains the SHAPE of Experiment 3's degradation curve, from 4 independent angles. (1) Direct linear-interaction regression (error^2 ~ k + acf1 + k*acf1, n=2,097,410): interaction term added ~0 R^2 (0.0645->0.0645) -- looked like a null result. (2) AR(1) theoretical model (parameter-free, driven only by each ACF-quartile's rho/sigma): explains R^2=0.448 of the empirical curve's variance across all quartile x k points -- strong, mechanistic evidence of real interaction. (3) Finer 10-way ACF-decile stratification: RMSE decreases monotonically D1->D10 at 9/9 values of k -- a genuine smooth relationship, not a quartile-binning artifact. (4) ACF vs. volatility (sigma) confound check: correlate at only r=-0.141 (largely independent signals); adding sigma + its own k-interaction on top of the ACF-only model adds +0.0462 R^2 (+71.6% relative) -- a bigger driver than the ACF interaction itself. RESOLUTION of the (1) vs (2)/(3) apparent conflict: the true k x ACF relationship is NONLINEAR (AR(1)'s rho^k form), so a raw multiplicative k*acf1 term is the wrong functional form and understates the effect -- a null result from a linear test should not be read as 'no interaction' when a mechanistic nonlinear model and a nonparametric decile check both say otherwise. VERDICT: PARTIALLY -- real, but not linear. Direct implication for ARCHITECTURE.md's StateSnapshot schema: months_since_observation alone is not the right state variable in isolation; keeping acf_1_3_6_12 and location_signature (mean/std) as distinct fields is empirically justified, and Project Phase 4 should test an explicit AR(1)-motivated composite feature (sigma*sqrt(2*(1-rho**k))), not just a raw product term, alongside letting the GBM learn the interaction natively via splits. Also fixed a real bug in the notebook-execution harness during this experiment: the resume logic could silently use a stale checkpoint namespace (NameError on later cells) when the harness's OUTPUTS_JSON got ahead of the actual dill-committed state after a mid-dump kill -- fixed with an explicit, atomically-written committed-cell-index sidecar file, plus explicit memory-hygiene cleanup (del + gc.collect on several multi-hundred-MB transient copies: pre2015, gpre/gpre_worst, indep, clean, full_sorted, records_A/B) that cut peak checkpoint size roughly in half. Docs updated: ASSUMPTIONS.md new A-010 (Validated, nonlinear form), PROJECT_PLAN.md Experiment 5 checkbox marked complete with full findings.

notebooks/02_forecastability.ipynb section 15-16. Compared train vs test distributions of SPEI (4 timescales), soil moisture, calendar month, and masking rate, per PROJECT_PLAN.md's Experiment 6 brief, framed explicitly as indirect (not direct) evidence for A-003 (spatial relationship stability is a different claim than marginal-covariate stability). Findings: (1) masking rate 0% (train) vs 66.5% (test) -- the single largest covariate-regime difference by construction, already the project's central design focus, not a new risk. (2) SPEI/soil moisture, train vs all of test: minimal shift, largest KS statistic 0.0352 (SOIL_MOISTURE_t), all 5 variables KS<0.04. (3) SPEI/soil moisture, test-unmasked vs test-masked rows (same test period): also minimal, largest KS 0.0569 -- the blackout regime is not meaningfully environmentally distinct from the observed regime within test, consistent with A-001's masking-as-hardware-gap account rather than an environmental one. (4) Calendar-month coverage: test entirely omits October (0/18 test months), and has ~2x the row-share for calendar months that recur twice within the 18 months (Jan/Feb/Mar/Jun/Jul/Sep/Dec) vs months appearing once (Apr/May/Aug/Nov) -- verified by hand against DATA_DICTIONARY.md's exact 18-month list, confirms the pattern is real, not a bug. VERDICT: covariate shift on SPEI/soil moisture is NOT the dominant generalization risk (masking-regime shift dwarfs it and is already addressed by the state-reconstruction architecture); the calendar-month coverage gap IS a real, actionable secondary risk for Phase 2 fold design and Phase 4 seasonal features. Docs updated: ASSUMPTIONS.md A-003 evidence strengthened (kept Active, indirect evidence only), new A-011 (Active) for the calendar-month coverage risk, PROJECT_PLAN.md Experiment 6 checkbox marked complete with full findings.

column15: notebooks/02_forecastability.ipynb section 17-18. Dedicated, properly-sourced external research (NOT a repeat of Experiment 1's single-search preview): JPL GRACE Tellus official site, JPL mission pages, and a peer-reviewed paper (Landerer et al. 2020, Geophysical Research Letters). Key sourced dates: GRACE launched 2002-03-17; battery-management outages since 2011 (~every 6 months, 4-8 weeks); GRACE-2 accelerometer off Oct 2016; last usable GRACE ranging data June 2017 (JPL also separately states 'ended science mission October 2017' -- both reported, not conflated); GRACE-FO launched 2018-05-22, first monthly fields June 2018; Landerer et al. describe an '11-month gap' with no detectable intermission bias. Three cross-checks against real data (not just narrative comparison): (1) grouped test's absent months into contiguous RUNS (fixed a real bug in an earlier draft of this cross-check that naively took min/max over non-contiguous absent months, implying false contiguity) -- the single longest run (2017-07 to 2018-06, 12 months) matches the documented 11-month gap exactly plus one extra month (2018-06, GRACE-FO's own first/commissioning-adjacent month) -- a near-exact, well-evidenced match. (2) 17/22 missing TRAINING months (2011 onward, 8 events, ~2/year, 1-2 month runs) match the documented battery-management cadence -- resolves a gap A-001 previously flagged as unexplained; 5 pre-2011 months remain unexplained. (3) 4 smaller absent runs also exist in the test period beyond the main gap -- only one (2016-10 to 2016-11) has a plausible sourced explanation (coincides with the GRACE-2 accelerometer shutdown); the other 3 don't align with any specific sourced event and are explicitly flagged as an open item (possibly Zindi's own month-selection choices), not force-fit into the narrative. VERDICT: A-001 formally upgraded Active->Validated on finding (1) alone; findings (2)-(3) are bonus/honest-open-items. Docs updated: ASSUMPTIONS.md A-001 upgraded to Validated, new A-012 (Active, low priority) recording the two genuinely open narrow items, PROJECT_PLAN.md Experiment 7 checkbox marked complete with full findings and Project Phase 1 Definition of Done marked MET.
